stories.headline: After Kulgam terror attack, Farooq Abdullah advocates "path of dialogue" with Pakistan
stories.title: After Kulgam terror attack, Farooq Abdullah advocates "path of dialogue" with Pakistan
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 12 : Jammu and Kashmir National Conference president Farooq Abdullah on Thursday called on Pakistan to end terrorism and choose dialogue to resolve outstanding issues, amid a spate of security incidents in Jammu and Kashmir, including the killing of two Special Police Officers (SPOs) in Kishtwar. Abdullah said terrorism should not intimidate people and reiterated that Kashmir was, is and will always remain a part of India. He also emphasised the need to revive the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) to facilitate dialogue and regional cooperation. "Terrorism exists, but we must not be intimidated by it. Kashmir was, is, and will always remain a part of India... I have always told Pakistan: put an end to terrorism. Terrorism will lead nowhere. Choose the path of dialogue; that is the only way a solution can be found. We were once part of the same nation... We must revive SAARC so that we can all sit together, resolve our issues, and move toward progress," he said. Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) MLA Aga Syed Muntazir Mehdi strongly condemned the attack on CRPF personnel in Kulgam on Wednesday and the killing of two SPOs in Kishtwar, while questioning the Central Government's approach towards Kashmir. He said violence had no place in a civilised or democratic society and stressed that controlling the visible signs of instability could not be considered a permanent solution. "We strongly condemn yesterday’s attack in Kulgam and the incident reported in Kishtwar today. Violence has no place in a civilised or democratic society. However, these repeated incidents raise serious questions about the Central Government’s approach towards Kashmir... The government may have controlled the visible signs of instability, but control is not a permanent solution," Mehdi said. In Kulgam district, a massive cordon and search operation (CASO) continued on Thursday after unidentified motorcycle-borne assailants opened fire on CRPF personnel deployed at a security checkpoint in Nowpora Akhran on Wednesday. The attack took place at around 2:15 pm, when the assailants opened fire on the security personnel before fleeing the spot. Three CRPF personnel sustained injuries in the firing and were shifted to a hospital in Anantnag district for treatment. In another incident from Kishtwar, the bullet-riddled bodies of the two SPOs, identified as Babi Chand (57) and Rashpal Kumar (45), were recovered on Thursday morning, a day after they went missing in the remote Dachhan belt. The two personnel were posted with the Special Operations Group (SOG) of the local police at Kiyar village in Dachhan. They had gone missing on Wednesday while travelling from their camp towards an Army post at Dharna-Marwah. Kishtwar MLA Shagun Parihar expressed grief over the killings, stating that the bodies of the two personnel were recovered at around 8 am and 9 am, respectively. "Regarding the incident in which two SPOs (Special Police Officers) were reportedly killed—what are your thoughts? It is a truly tragic incident. Two of our SPOs from the southern region have been killed. They had gone missing last night, and their bodies were recovered this morning—one around 8:00 AM and the other around 9:00 AM. It is deeply saddening," Parihar said. (ANI)

stories.headline: Cyclone Murasu damages 143 fishing boats at Gundamala village in Prakasam district
stories.title: Cyclone Murasu damages 143 fishing boats at Gundamala village in Prakasam district
stories.summary: Fisheries Department officials yet to assess the overall value of the damages; the boats were moored amid the mangrove forests but collided with each other and sustained damages due to the strong gale-force winds and heavy rains triggered by the cyclone
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Several fishing boats were damaged due to Cyclone Murasu in the coastal village of Gundamala in Kothapatnam mandal of Prakasam district.
The officials of the Fisheries Department have not yet assessed the overall value of the damages.
The fiber boats belonging to the local fishermen were moored amid the mangrove forests, where seawater meets a small stretch of Buckingham Canal.
They collided with each other and sustained damages due to the strong gale-force winds and heavy rains triggered by the cyclone.
Currently, the boats remain trapped among the mangrove vegetation.
The heavy machinery used for the installation of electricity poles has been causing delay in the efforts of the fishermen to bring their boats back into the canal.
There are approximately 450 fishermen in the village.
Meanwhile, the local fishermen informed that the earth-moving equipment operators were charging ₹10,000 to retrieve each large boat and ₹6,000 for each small boat.
Of the 164 fishing boats in the village, 143 were damaged, including 15 large and 25 medium-sized boats.

stories.headline: RBI rate hike in December: SBI now expects just 25 bps despite inflation crossing 6%
stories.title: RBI rate hike in December: SBI now expects just 25 bps despite inflation crossing 6%
stories.summary: In its latest Ecowrap report dated November 12, SBI Research said the balance of probabilities had shifted decisively towards a smaller rate increase at the Reserve Bank of India's December Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'monetary policy' in summary weight 24
article_sentences: The revision comes after India's consumer price index (CPI) inflation climbed to a two-year high of 6.09% in October, exceeding the RBI's upper tolerance limit for the first time under the new CPI series.
“When facts change, I change my mind.
What do you do sir?” the SBI Research report stated, as it revised its December rate hike forecast from 50 basis points to 25 basis points.

Earlier, the research team had outlined two possibilities: an aggressive 50-bps hike or a 25-bps repo rate increase accompanied by another 25-bps tightening through widening the interest rate corridor.
However, recent domestic and international developments have strengthened the case for a more measured response.
SBI identified four developments behind its revised forecast.
First, the RBI's efforts to stabilise the rupee and ease liquidity pressures have yielded results.
The currency recovered below ₹94 against the dollar before weakening again, while overnight money market rates moderated.
Second, improving foreign capital flows could reduce pressure on the currency.
SBI noted foreign institutional investment inflows of approximately $7.68 billion since November 4, alongside a 0.7% appreciation in the rupee.
Third, easing geopolitical tensions have improved the crude oil outlook.
Brent crude prices have declined approximately 11% following the US elections, potentially reducing India's imported inflation pressures.

stories.headline: India's retail inflation crosses RBI's upper limit of 6 per cent in October
stories.title: India's retail inflation crosses RBI's upper limit of 6 per cent in October
stories.summary: Overall food inflation in October stood at 8.94 per cent as the prices of onions shot up by 116.22 per cent while garlic turned costlier by 60.74 per cent.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Overall food inflation in October stood at 8.94 per cent as the prices of onions shot up by 116.22 per cent while garlic turned costlier by 60.74 per cent.

New Delhi: India's retail inflation, based on the new Consumer Price Index (CPI) series, rose to 6.09 per cent in October this year compared to the same month of the previous year to cross the RBI's upper limit for the first time after two years, according to data released by the Ministry of Statistics on Thursday.
Ginger and lemon prices also rose by 48.32 per cent and 47.30 per cent, respectively, during the month.

On the other hand, potato prices fell by 14.24 per cent during the month, while cauliflower and coconut turned cheaper by 10.57 per cent and 5.6 per cent, respectively, in October compared to the same month of the previous year.
Silver jewellery was among the commodities that posted the highest inflation during the month, with prices surging as much as 52.39 per cent.
The CPI inflation has breached the upper limit of the RBI safe zone, raising expectations of a rate hike by the RBI in the next monetary policy review.
The tolerance zone of the RBI ranges from 2 per cent to 6 per cent.
The RBI's monetary policy aims to keep inflation within this zone as it balances its objective of promoting economic growth with stability.
The monetary policy committee voted unanimously to increase the policy repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5 per cent on October 7.
Acceleration of inflation in key economies has prompted a shift towards hawkish monetary policy.
The US Fed hiked by 25 bps in September.
RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said in the monetary policy statement on October 7 that CPI inflation increased to 4.8 per cent in August 2026 from 4.5 per cent in July.

stories.headline: India’s retail inflation rises to 6.09% in October, breaches RBI’s upper tolerance limit
stories.title: India’s retail inflation rises to 6.09% in October, breaches RBI’s upper tolerance limit
stories.summary: Higher food costs, particularly for vegetables, pushed consumer prices up, adding to the monetary policy challenge ahead of the December review.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'monetary policy' in summary weight 24
article_sentences: India’s retail inflation, measured by the Consumer Price Index (CPI), rose to 6.09 per cent in October 2026 from 5.54 per cent in September, marking its highest level since October 2024, when it stood at 6.21 per cent, according to data released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation on Thursday.
The latest reading represents a 55-basis-point increase over the previous month and takes inflation above the RBI’s upper tolerance limit of 6 per cent.
The central bank’s inflation-targeting framework mandates maintaining CPI inflation at 4 per cent, with a tolerance band of 2 per cent to 6 per cent.
Rural food inflation stood at 9.09 per cent, while urban food inflation was recorded at 8.68 per cent.
At the national level, inflation in the food and beverages category stood at 8.51 per cent.
Personal care, social protection and miscellaneous goods and services recorded inflation of 10.14 per cent, while restaurants and accommodation services saw a rise of 10.06 per cent.
Among individual food items, onion prices recorded inflation of 116.22 per cent in October, compared with 108.13 per cent in September.
Garlic inflation rose to 60.74 per cent from 54.62 per cent during the same period.
Rural inflation increased to 6.63 per cent in October from 6.08 per cent in September, while urban inflation rose to 5.41 per cent from 4.88 per cent.
The inflation reading comes after the RBI raised the policy repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50 per cent at its October policy review and shifted its stance to calibrated tightening.
The December 2-4 meeting will be the next opportunity for the MPC to assess the implications of rising price pressures for monetary policy.

stories.headline: Cabinet approves ₹62,370-crore fertiliser subsidy for Rabi season
stories.title: Cabinet approves ₹62,370-crore fertiliser subsidy for Rabi season
stories.summary: The package includes Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) rates for phosphatic and potassic (P&K) fertilisers for the period October 1, 2026, to March 31, 2027.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a fertiliser subsidy package of Rs 62,370 crore for the Rabi 2026-27 season, a 64 per cent increase over the Rs 37,952 crore allocated for the previous Rabi season, with provisions to keep Di-ammonium Phosphate (DAP) available to farmers at a fixed price of Rs 1,350 per bag.
The package includes Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) rates for phosphatic and potassic (P&K) fertilisers for the period October 1, 2026, to March 31, 2027.

It also provides for special assistance for DAP, extension of these provisions to Triple Superphosphate (TSP) and Monoammonium Phosphate (MAP), freight subsidy for Single Superphosphate (SSP), and continuation of subsidy on ammonium sulphate.
The enhanced outlay comes against the backdrop of global fertiliser price volatility and disruptions arising from the West Asia crisis.
The government said the package would ensure adequate availability of fertilisers during the Rabi season, while keeping input costs stable for farmers.
Under the approved NBS rates, the subsidy has been fixed at Rs 94.21 per kg for nitrogen, Rs 66.11 per kg for phosphorus, Rs 2.38 per kg for potash and Rs 10.42 per kg for sulphur.
The government will continue special provisions beyond the NBS framework to ensure DAP is available at Rs 1,350 per bag.
These provisions have also been extended to imported and domestic TSP and imported MAP.
The freight subsidy on SSP will continue during the Rabi season to encourage its use as an affordable alternative to DAP.
The subsidy on imported and domestic ammonium sulphate will also be continued.
In a push to strengthen domestic production and reduce import dependence, the Cabinet has also approved a sulphur package for domestic manufacturers.
Under this, manufacturers will receive 20 per cent of the actual procurement cost of sulphur, subject to a floor price of $800 per tonne.

stories.headline: Technological superiority key to enhancing operational readiness against emerging threats: Rajanth Singh
stories.title: Technological superiority key to enhancing operational readiness against emerging threats: Rajanth Singh
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 12: Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has called upon the Defence Forces to strengthen and sustain both offensive and defensive dimensions of the ‘element of surprise’ to maintain operational readiness against conventional and emerging threats arising from rapid technological advancements and the evolving nature of modern warfare. Addressing the Air Force Commanders’ Conference in New Delhi on November 12, 2026, he emphasised the need to continue bolstering intelligence and surveillance capabilities, enhance integration among systems and identify potential threats before they unfold. “Our Defence Forces must develop capabilities and methods that leave the adversary with no time to react or recover, while simultaneously ensuring that we are never caught off guard by an unexpected move from the enemy. Surprise can manifest in various forms, both conventional and electronic. Our intelligence and surveillance mechanisms must be further strengthened and operational preparedness enhanced to ensure that our personnel remain alert, agile and equipped to respond effectively to any emerging challenge,” said the Raksha Mantri. Shri Rajnath Singh asserted that contemporary conflicts are extending beyond traditional battlefields into non-contact domains, with missiles, drones and advanced weapon systems playing a significant role. Referring to the Russia-Ukraine and Israel-Hamas conflicts, he stated that drones and air defence systems have emerged as critical components of modern warfare. He exhorted the Commanders to remain prepared for emerging challenges such as kamikaze drones, surveillance and counter-drone operations. Raksha Mantri called upon the Indian Air Force (IAF) to develop dedicated doctrines and architectures for emerging domains of warfare, including electronic, cyber and space. He emphasised that enhanced preparedness in these domains would strengthen the ability to address future challenges. “Victory in future conflicts would depend not merely on the number of aircraft, but also on technological sophistication, speed of response and precision of preparations,” he said, urging the Commanders to make these emerging challenges a core priority, with focus on integrating them into institutional thinking, planning and operational processes. Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted that the Defence Forces are undergoing a transformative phase, encompassing reforms in wide-ranging areas, including organisational structures, jointness & integration, and operational concepts. He added that the changing security environment necessitated continuous adaptation and a forward-looking approach to military preparedness. Raksha Mantri commended the IAF for effectively implementing its doctrines and operational methods during and after Operation Sindoor, appreciating the professionalism, restraint & judgement demonstrated by the air warriors in successfully executing their assigned tasks. He stated that the lessons learnt during the operation were clearly reflected in the IAF's evolving operational procedures, particularly through the increased emphasis on drones and air defence systems, which are vital to national security. These lessons, he added, are shaping the pace and direction of the transformative changes underway in the Defence Forces. Highlighting the coordinated and complementary contributions of all the three Services effectively demonstrated during Op Sindoor, Shri Rajnath Singh congratulated the Defence Forces for the synergy and integration. He underlined that jointness and integrated efforts must continue to guide military planning and operational execution. While appreciating the IAF for enhancing the skills and capabilities of its personnel in keeping with rapid technological advancements, Raksha Mantri urged the Commanders to sustain efforts towards training air warriors in emerging technologies. He underscored the importance of leveraging the technological knowledge and expertise of young recruits, stating that their capabilities could contribute significantly to stronger decision-making and organisational development. On the Second Tour of Duty for Agniveers, Shri Rajnath Singh stated that the decision was taken following feedback received from the Defence Forces, reiterating the Government's commitment to incorporating the Services’ suggestions into policy decisions. He expressed confidence that the ‘Second Tour of Duty’ initiative would contribute to further bolstering the three Services. As part of this conference, Raksha Mantri launched a suite of Artificial Intelligence (Al) applications developed in-house by the IAF's Al Centre of Excellence of the Unit for Digitisation, Automation, Artificial Intelligence and Application Networking (UDAAN). The applications will be utilised to automate and expedite tasks across the domains of operations, administration and aerospace safety, and are deployed on the IAF’s secure network. The initiative marks a significant milestone in the IAF's pursuit of technology-driven transformation and enhanced operational capabilities. The inaugural session was also attended by Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth, Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh, Secretary (Defence Production) Shri Sanjeev Kumar, and Secretary (Defence Finance) Shri Vishvajit Sahay. Air Officers Commanding-in-Chief of all Commands of IAF, all Principal Staff Officers & all Director Generals. The two-day conference is being attended by the Air Officers Commanding-in-Chief of all Commands of IAF, all Principal Staff Officers & all Director Generals. The conference provides a forum to the senior leadership of the IAF to discuss critical issues pertaining to operations, maintenance and administration.

opening: New Delhi, Nov 12: Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has called upon the Defence Forces to strengthen and sustain both offensive and defensive dimensions of the ‘element of surprise’ to maintain operational readiness against conventional and emerging threats arising from rapid technological advancements and the evolving nature of modern warfare.

Addressing the Air Force Commanders’ Conference in New Delhi on November 12, 2026, he emphasised the need to continue bolstering intelligence and surveillance capabilities, enhance integration among systems and identify potential threats before they unfold.
body: “Our Defence Forces must develop capabilities and methods that leave the adversary with no time to react or recover, while simultaneously ensuring that we are never caught off guard by an unexpected move from the enemy.
Surprise can manifest in various forms, both conventional and electronic.

Our intelligence and surveillance mechanisms must be further strengthened and operational preparedness enhanced to ensure that our personnel remain alert, agile and equipped to respond effectively to any emerging challenge,” said the Raksha Mantri.

Shri Rajnath Singh asserted that contemporary conflicts are extending beyond traditional battlefields into non-contact domains, with missiles, drones and advanced weapon systems playing a significant role.
Referring to the Russia-Ukraine and Israel-Hamas conflicts, he stated that drones and air defence systems have emerged as critical components of modern warfare.
He exhorted the Commanders to remain prepared for emerging challenges such as kamikaze drones, surveillance and counter-drone operations.
Raksha Mantri called upon the Indian Air Force (IAF) to develop dedicated doctrines and architectures for emerging domains of warfare, including electronic, cyber and space.
He emphasised that enhanced preparedness in these domains would strengthen the ability to address future challenges.

“Victory in future conflicts would depend not merely on the number of aircraft, but also on technological sophistication, speed of response and precision of preparations,” he said, urging the Commanders to make these emerging challenges a core priority, with focus on integrating them into institutional thinking, planning and operational processes.

Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted that the Defence Forces are undergoing a transformative phase, encompassing reforms in wide-ranging areas, including organisational structures, jointness & integration, and operational concepts.
He added that the changing security environment necessitated continuous adaptation and a forward-looking approach to military preparedness.

Raksha Mantri commended the IAF for effectively implementing its doctrines and operational methods during and after Operation Sindoor, appreciating the professionalism, restraint & judgement demonstrated by the air warriors in successfully executing their assigned tasks.

He stated that the lessons learnt during the operation were clearly reflected in the IAF's evolving operational procedures, particularly through the increased emphasis on drones and air defence systems, which are vital to national security.
These lessons, he added, are shaping the pace and direction of the transformative changes underway in the Defence Forces.

Highlighting the coordinated and complementary contributions of all the three Services effectively demonstrated during Op Sindoor, Shri Rajnath Singh congratulated the Defence Forces for the synergy and integration.
He underlined that jointness and integrated efforts must continue to guide military planning and operational execution.

While appreciating the IAF for enhancing the skills and capabilities of its personnel in keeping with rapid technological advancements, Raksha Mantri urged the Commanders to sustain efforts towards training air warriors in emerging technologies.

He underscored the importance of leveraging the technological knowledge and expertise of young recruits, stating that their capabilities could contribute significantly to stronger decision-making and organisational development.

On the Second Tour of Duty for Agniveers, Shri Rajnath Singh stated that the decision was taken following feedback received from the Defence Forces, reiterating the Government's commitment to incorporating the Services’ suggestions into policy decisions.
He expressed confidence that the ‘Second Tour of Duty’ initiative would contribute to further bolstering the three Services.

As part of this conference, Raksha Mantri launched a suite of Artificial Intelligence (Al) applications developed in-house by the IAF's Al Centre of Excellence of the Unit for Digitisation, Automation, Artificial Intelligence and Application Networking (UDAAN).
The applications will be utilised to automate and expedite tasks across the domains of operations, administration and aerospace safety, and are deployed on the IAF’s secure network.
The initiative marks a significant milestone in the IAF's pursuit of technology-driven transformation and enhanced operational capabilities.

The inaugural session was also attended by Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth, Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh, Secretary (Defence Production) Shri Sanjeev Kumar, and Secretary (Defence Finance) Shri Vishvajit Sahay.

stories.headline: India's Ambekar Meetei scripts history with boxing gold at Dakar Youth Olympics
stories.title: India's Ambekar Meetei scripts history with boxing gold at Dakar Youth Olympics
stories.summary: Lairenlakpam Ambekar Meetei made history at Dakar 2026 by clinching the gold medal in the men's 50kg boxing category, edging out Ireland’s Kristian Jubani in a nail-biting 3-2 final. His path to glory included a resounding 5-0 victory over Colombia's Izzon Jeffrey Galea Arevalo. This achievement signifies a significant moment for Indian sports, breaking a 16-year streak without an Indian boxer in the finals of the Youth Olympic Games.
